title: The Growing Power of the Behavioral Sciences
coreMove: Ask who controls behavioral knowledge and whether its use enlarges or diminishes personal freedom.
sourcePressure: Rogers weighs the promise and danger of behavioral-science power as it becomes more capable of shaping human lives. No split source sidecar exists for ch20; frozen TOC and book skeleton support the heading, part placement, and broad intent only, with no chapter-local named anecdotes, studies, or places.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Making behavioral science either savior or villain.
sourceAnchorNote: The frozen source exposes no usable chapter-local named person, study, institution, place, date, or anecdotal artifact from Rogers here. Use fictional protagonists only; do not invent named Rogers cases or studies.
